name: Jediael
overview: Jediael was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh who played a significant military role as a captain of thousands. He is noted for defecting to David and joining him at Ziklag, demonstrating loyalty during a critical period in David's rise to kingship. His leadership position highlights his importance among those who supported David.
namesAndTitles: The name Jediael means 'known of G-d [El],' reflecting a recognition of divine acknowledgment. This proper name, as recorded, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful theophoric element pointing to God's knowledge or recognition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jediael was a descendant of Manasseh, linking him to one of the tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Jediael's significance lies in his role as a leader who joined David at Ziklag with a contingent of thousands, symbolizing the growing support for David among the tribes of Israel. His defection from other factions to David's cause illustrates the shifting allegiances that were crucial for David's eventual establishment as king. This moment reflects God's providential guidance in raising up leaders who recognized and supported His anointed.
